title: Optimizing a matmul, in order
summary: The usual path from a naive CUDA matmul to one near cuBLAS.

items.text: Use vectorized loads and double-buffer the shared tiles so the next tile loads while this one computes.
Stage `BM × BK` and `BK × BN` tiles in shared memory, with a barrier per tile.
Move the inner product to Tensor Core instructions (WMMA, MMA or a library such as CUTLASS) with BF16 or FP16 inputs.
One thread per output element, reading a row of `A` and a column of `B` from global memory.
Give each thread a small tile of outputs in registers (for example 8 × 8), reusing each shared-memory value several times.
Map threads so that consecutive threads write consecutive columns of `C`, making the loads of `B` coalesce.
